checks_passed.what_was_verified: The patent prints no product mass anywhere, only percentage yields, so no mass/mole/yield triple exists to close. I checked every printed charge pair against molecular weights instead: Example 2, Br2 0.616 mol against 0.583 mol of the 172.7 g/mol sulfide, 1.06 eq; Example 3, 23% H2O2 224 g gives 1.51 mol against 0.580 mol of the 251.6 g/mol bromide, ratio 2.6, which sits inside the 2 to 3 the patent itself prefers at line 275; Example 4 Method 1, Br2 1.12 eq, Method 2, NBS 1.22 eq on 0.296 mol of substrate; Example 5, NaH 0.23 mol, trifluoroethanol 0.24 mol, substrate 0.229 mol; Example 9, dione 0.262 mol against 0.248 mol of substrate, 1.06 eq; Example 11, dione 1.31 eq. Nothing implies an impossible molecular weight, so mass_balance_implausible correctly appears on no record, and no record carries it falsely.

Example 2 charges 100.75 g of the formula (VI) sulfide, 0.583 mol, whose theoretical maximum of the formula (I) bromide is 146.8 g; Example 3 charges 146 g of it, inside that ceiling at 99.4%. Example 3's 146 g caps the formula (II) sulfone at 164.6 g and Example 4 charges 84 g. Example 4's 84 g caps the formula (III) bromide at 107.4 g and Example 5 charges 83 g. No step consumes more than the previous can supply, so scale_discontinuity correctly appears on no record.

The complaint from another artifact's audit does not hold at source. Rule 21 bins on the limiting reagent charge, lab 1 to 100 g and pilot 100 g to 10 kg. Example 1's limiting reagent is the 100 g of 3-chloro-2-methylaniline, 0.706 mol against 0.729 mol of NaNO2, so it falls in lab; the 1165 g of 5.1% hydrochloric acid is a dilute solution mass, not a reagent charge. Example 2 charges 100.75 g and Example 3 charges 146 g of their limiting reagents, both above the 100 g boundary, so pilot is correct for both. The apparent oddity is the bin edge sitting at exactly 100 g, not a mis-set field.
